1

 Judgment

Challenging the quantum of compensaation awarded by the Tribunal in MCOP.No.6338 of 2019 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes, Chennai, the appellant/insurance company has come forward with this appeal.
2.The learned counsel for the appellant insurance company sumitted that the accident occured on 18.09.2019 and that at the time of the accident, the victim of the accident was 26 years old.
He was a B.Com. Gratuate and had also completed MBA.,

In the claim statement of the mother of the deceased, she has stated that the victim was working in a company and was earning Rs.12,000/- per month and that he left the job in the year 2017 and till the time of the accident which occurred in the year 2019, for about 2 years he was not working anywhere.
However, he used to go for work on daily wages, which depends upon the availability of the work.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

3.Therefore, the learned counsel would submit that for the accident, which occurred in the year 2019, without any valid proof of income, the Tribunal ought not to have fixed Rs.18,000/- as the notional monthly income of the deceased.

Further, fixation of the notional income at Rs.18,000/-,
when the victim's mother has stated in the claim statement that he was earning Rs.12,000/- in 2017,
is not appropriate.
Therefore, he would suggest that Rs.12,000/- may be fixed as the notional income of the deceased.
He would however, submit that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under other heads of compensation are just and reasonable and that the same may be cofirmed.

4.On the other hand, the learned counsel appearing for the first respondent/claimant would submit that in similar cases this Court as well as the Apex Court has fixed the notional income even for a second year college student at Rs.18,000/- and therefore, the same yardstick may be followed in the present case and requires to comfirm the award passed by the Tribunal, without any modification or alteration.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
5.I have given due consideration to the submissions of the learned counsel for the appellant and the first respondent and perused the materials available on record.
6.There is no dispute with regard to the manner in which the accident occured or fixation of negligence and fastening the liability.
The dipuste is only with regard to the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
In the present case, the accident occurred on 18.09.2019 and the deceased was about 26 years old at the relevant time.
In the claim statement, the claimant has stated that the victim was earning Rs.12,000/- per month.
However, at the time of filing proof affidavt, she has stated that the victim was earning about Rs.30,000/-.

However, in the cross- examination, the appellant has culled out from the claimant that her son was not at all working anywhere at the time of the accident and he was doing temporary works, on and off, for daily wages,
whenever the work was available, contradiction to the statement made in the claim statement and the proof affidavit.
The Tribunal however, has fixed the notional income of the victim of the accident at Rs.18,000/-.

https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Also At vs Seetha Lakshmi on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72389446/
2 7.When there is contradiction in the claim statement and the proof affidavit, and the respondent has culled out in the cross-examination of the claimant that the victim was not working at the time of the accident
, the Tribunal ought not to have fixed the notional income of the victim of the accident at Rs.18,000/-.
In case the victim was an efficient person and was able to get employment, this Court would have considered awarding a higher sum as the notional income of the deceased.
However, in the present case, the victim lost his job in 2017 and he was not able to get any employment, which shows his ability to get employment.
In these circumstances, the fixation of the notional income at Rs.18,000/- by the Tribunal is on the higher side.
8.Considering the above aspects, this Court now fixes the notional income of the deceased at Rs.16,000/- instead of Rs.18,000/- as fixed by the Tribunal.

Accordingly, the compensation determined by the Tribunal is redetermined as below;

1. Loss of 25,70,400/- 22,84,800/ R  Dependency -
2 . Towards Loss of 15,000/- 15,000/- Co  Estate  3. Towards Loss of 40,000/- 40,000/- Co  Consortium
4. Towards Funeral 15,000/- 15,000/- Co  Expenses

https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 10.In the result, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is partly allowed and the compensation awarded by the Tribunal at Rs.26,40,400/- is hereby Reduced to Rs.23,54,800/- together with interest at the Also At vs Seetha Lakshmi on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72389446/
3 rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

The Appellant-Insurance Company is directed to deposit the award amount now determined by this Court, along with interest and costs, less the amount already deposited, if any, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment to the credit of M.C.O.P.No. 6338 of 2019 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes, Chennai.
On such deposit being made, the Tribunal is directed to transfer the Award amount, directly to the Bank account of the Claimant/1st respondent through RTGS, within a period of three weeks.
No costs.
Consequently, the connected miscellaneous petition is closed.
